clue.text: Tricky moves nan and son played in Scrabble?

definitions.text: nan and son played in Scrabble?

blocks.note: first meaning: awkward manoeuvres that turn a car round in a narrow road

blocks.clueFragment: nan and son played in Scrabble?
blocks.note: second meaning: each of these words scores three points on the board, so playing them is a turn worth that much

explanation.surface: Granny and her boy play cunning moves in a family game of Scrabble.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scrabble N, A, S and O are each worth one point, so NAN and SON score three apiece; each go in the game is a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers reverse a vehicle in three separate manoeuvres to face the other way, a test of skill on narrow roads.

clue.text: Hit on server, wanting one free drink

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the server's word loses its single letter i

blocks.note: to tap is to strike lightly
a waiter serves at table

explanation.surface: A customer strikes the waiter and is refused one of the free drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit on' suggests flirting with the waiter, but on simply puts one piece first in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the household faucet costs nothing in a restaurant, unlike bottled mineral varieties.

clue.text: Greek character to keep so long in Spain with programme?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the farewell sits within the letter

blocks.note: the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet
Spanish for goodbye
W is a standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A Greek letter is supposed to say a lengthy Spanish farewell on a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast on the wireless is a programme, the usual sense of a show on air.

clue.text: Base on Greek island reportedly crumbles

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the island's name is taken by its sound

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
Rhodes is a Dodecanese island

explanation.surface: A military base on a Greek island is said to be falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a foundation or camp, but it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, and something that erodes crumbles bit by bit.

clue.text: Initial lack of judgement's possibly done MP in

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement out of many, so the letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician has been stitched up by a hasty verdict before the facts came out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without preconceptions has not yet reached a verdict, so it is a deliberate absence of early opinion.

clue.text: Some plutocrat fancied overturning old trade deal

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is wanted
in a down entry overturning turns the run of letters upside down, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A rich man who took a liking to scrapping a former trade pact.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ATFAN inside plutocrat fancied, read upwards, gives NAFTA.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American Free Trade Agreement of 1994 was replaced by a newer pact in 2020.

clue.text: Somehow neat duet made tighter

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unspecified method, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Two musicians somehow sharpened their tidy duet.
explanation.definitionFit: To tauten is to pull something taut, stretching a rope or wire so it is less slack.

clue.text: Free kicks regularly taken by Methuselah in energetic practice

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
Methuselah is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter takes free kicks regularly as part of a lively training regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' simply attaches the setter's I after the selected letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Reiki is a Japanese healing technique said to channel life energy through the practitioner's hands.

clue.text: Quiet PM sent up distress signal

indicators.note: in a down entry sent up means the name travels upwards, read from bottom to top

blocks.note: sh is the call for silence
Keir Starmer, the UK Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A quiet Prime Minister fired off a flare for help.
explanation.definitionFit: A piercing scream is a cry that signals fear or alarm, so it works as a call for help.

clue.text: Boss's secretary given buzzer that doesn't work

blocks.note: PA is a personal assistant
a male bee does no work in the hive

explanation.surface: The boss's secretary has been handed an intercom buzzer that is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzzer that doesn't work' sounds like a faulty bell, but it is a male bee, which gathers no nectar.
explanation.definitionFit: Padrone is Italian for a master or employer, used in English for a proprietor or patron.

clue.text: Mathematician's delivery person getting the wrong entrance

indicators.note: an entrance is a way in, here the opening letter, and the wrong one swaps it for another

blocks.note: a courier delivers parcels

explanation.surface: A mathematician's delivery driver has gone in through the wrong door.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay only says the first letter is wrong; the crossing letters and the mathematician confirm F replaces C.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Fourier was a French mathematician known for the series that bears his name.

clue.text: Made up and in agreement with date

blocks.note: people at one are agreed
d is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Someone put on make-up and agreed to a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' looks like cosmetics or invention, but it means made amends.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up for a wrong is to make amends, and atoned is the past tense of that idea.

clue.text: 50s classic - presumably not the original recording

blocks.note: first meaning: the Dave Brubeck Quartet jazz standard of 1959
second meaning: read literally, the fifth attempt in a studio session

explanation.walkthrough: A take is one recorded attempt, so a numbered take beyond the first cannot be the original.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paul Desmond tune in five-four time is one of the best-selling jazz singles of the late fifties.

clue.text: See 4
One on the rebound is content to neck with hot love

indicators.note: the content of something is what lies inside it, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: the two inner letters
h for hot, as on taps
love is nil in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone just out of a relationship is happy to kiss a passionate lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rebound' suggests a jilted lover, but it is a sound bouncing back.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound comes back off a surface, so it literally rebounds to the listener.

clue.text: A bunch of retired coppers ordered penne in European resort

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh sequence, so the pasta letters are rearranged
in places the rearranged pasta inside the resort's name

blocks.note: Nice is on the French Riviera
the pasta's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Retired police officers order pasta while holidaying on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired coppers' look like former police, but they are old copper pennies withdrawn from use.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine old pennies were a sum of pre-decimal British coinage, a handful of the bronze coins.

clue.text: City welcoming a number being celebrated today? Grand!

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
the puzzle ran on 14 March, Pi Day

explanation.surface: A city throws a party for a celebrity, and it is grand.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi Day is 14 March, written 3/14 in the US style, echoing 3.14.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is slang for impressive or excellent, an exclamation much like saying great or splendid.

clue.text: Standard horror film skewering cornier novel

indicators.note: a skewer pierces through the middle, so one piece runs inside the other
novel means new, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the letters rearranged
It, the Stephen King horror

explanation.surface: A standard horror film cuts through a more hackneyed novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a principle or test by which things are judged, a yardstick or benchmark.

clue.text: Republic of Dagenham and Stanmore reduced by 50%

indicators.note: cut by half means only the front half of each place name survives

blocks.note: an east London district
a north-west London suburb

explanation.surface: Two London suburbs are cut in size, as if forming a new state.
explanation.walkthrough: Dagenham and Stanmore are London districts at opposite ends of the city; each keeps its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dagestan is a constituent republic of the Russian Federation on the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: A bunch of bare asses shocked judge again

indicators.note: a bunch is a part gathered from the following run of letters

blocks.note: a run of consecutive letters across the three words

explanation.surface: Bare bottoms shocked a judge into looking at the case again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocked' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters sit in order inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate once more, forming a fresh appraisal of something already judged.

clue.text: Old-fashioned denomination's terribly sad on entering bar

indicators.note: terribly means done badly, so the letters are jumbled
entering means going inside, so these letters sit within the bar

blocks.note: Twix is a chocolate bar
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned religious group is miserable about going into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denomination' suggests a church, but it is a coin value; a Twix is a chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Two shillings and sixpence was the half-crown, a value in pre-decimal British money.

clue.text: Female setter has X factor

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for female
the setter refers to himself as I
the contraction 've, as in I've

explanation.surface: A female crossword compiler has star quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X factor' sounds like the talent show, but X is the Roman ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten divides exactly by five, so this number is one of the divisors of the Roman numeral X.

clue.text: American actress set aside, losing Oscar record

indicators.note: Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for o, and losing it removes that letter

blocks.note: to store is to put by for later
an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An American actress is passed over and misses out on an Oscar for her record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing Oscar' looks like an awards snub, but it drops the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is an American film actress who has won three Academy Awards.

clue.text: Reject detective stitched up in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as it falls on the ear, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: DI is a detective inspector, and stitched is sewn

explanation.surface: A rejected detective was framed during a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stitched up' suggests framing, but it means sewn.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge any connection with someone, rejecting them completely.

clue.text: Blend of wheat and rye involving multiple parts

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters are combined in a new order

blocks.note: the two grains, with and as a link

explanation.surface: A mix of two grains has several components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two grains and adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something split among a trio of participants or directions involves several parts, three in this case.

clue.text: I Got You Babe ultimately covered by couples fronting rock groups

indicators.note: a couple is two, and fronting means at the head, so each word gives its first pair
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is used
covered by means wrapped within, so the single letter sits inside the others

blocks.note: the first two letters
the first two letters
the final letter

explanation.surface: A Sonny and Cher hit is covered by pairs leading rock bands.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter of Babe goes inside the second pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is radio-speak meaning message received and understood, the same as saying I understand you.

clue.text: Eastenders in churches concealing large mistakes

indicators.note: concealing hides from view, so the size abbreviation l disappears

blocks.note: lapses are slips or errors

explanation.surface: Residents of East London hide serious blunders in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastenders' suggests the London soap, but it means things at the east end of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded recess at the end of a church, traditionally built facing east.

clue.text: Notes provided around unfinished poems

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the conditional word is read backwards
unfinished means the end is missing, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: if means provided that
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Footnotes are supplied around some uncompleted poems.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiver is a five-pound banknote, so these are paper money rather than written jottings.

clue.text: European person putting son on throne

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for son
the throne is slang for the toilet

explanation.surface: A European monarch places his son on the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throne' looks royal, but it is jokey slang for a toilet; on means S comes first in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavs are speakers of Slavic languages across eastern and central Europe, such as Poles or Czechs.

clue.text: Small quantities of heroin shifted in lofty settings

indicators.note: shifted means moved to another spot, so the letters do not stay where they began

blocks.note: high places

explanation.surface: Drugs are moved about in elevated locations.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first H moves, to sit before the final S. 'heroin' could be the H of the wordplay, but it belongs to the definition: drugs are sold by the eighth of an ounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealers sell drugs in eighth-ounce bags, so eighths are standard small street amounts.

clue.text: Old pope maybe recalling one with pride

definitions.note: read as the name Leo Nine, a pope of the eleventh century

blocks.note: first meaning: Leo IX, pope from 1049 to 1054, split into his name and number
second meaning: resembling a lion, which lives in a pride

explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' suggests self-respect, but it is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means like a lion, and a lion is the animal that lives in a pride.

clue.text: School trips which caretakers are asked to go on

definitions.text: School trips which caretakers are asked to go on

blocks.clueFragment: School trips which caretakers are asked to go on
blocks.note: surface reading: school janitors invited along on outings
setter's reading: those who care for children, visiting school for meetings with teachers

explanation.walkthrough: 'caretakers' suggests school janitors and 'trips' outings, but they are mothers and fathers making visits to the school.
explanation.definitionFit: Schools hold evening sessions where guardians meet teachers to discuss their children's progress.
